title: Blockchain-Based intrusion detection system for IoMT utilizing an enhanced artificial bee colony (E-ABC) and deep belief network (DBN)

phase5_fulltext_reason: Included. The paper proposes a blockchain-enabled IoMT intrusion-detection framework that, according to its detailed methodology and Algorithm 3, combines an unsupervised autoencoder with a supervised Naive Bayes classifier. The autoencoder learns compressed representations and produces reconstruction errors used as anomaly scores. The encoded features and corresponding labels are then used to train Naive Bayes. During inference, a sample whose reconstruction loss exceeds a predefined threshold is labelled as an anomaly; otherwise, the Naive Bayes prediction is used. This constitutes an explicit multi-stage unsupervised–supervised IDS and satisfies IC3. E-ABC performs feature selection and parameter optimization but is not itself the anomaly detector. The paper should nevertheless be flagged for severe internal inconsistency: the title and abstract describe E-ABC with a Deep Belief Network, whereas the methodology, architecture diagram, Algorithm 3, results discussion, and conclusion implement and describe an Autoencoder–Naive Bayes model. The empirical evaluation also uses the generic NSL-KDD dataset rather than an IoMT-specific dataset.

The paper proposes an edge-based hybrid IoT botnet detection framework combining supervised classifiers, including Random Forest, SVM, and Decision Tree, with unsupervised anomaly-detection methods such as K-Means and Isolation Forest. The model outputs are combined through an ensemble and supported by Apache Kafka and Spark for distributed real-time processing. Although the architecture technically combines supervised and unsupervised detection components, it targets generic IoT ecosystems and is evaluated using CICIDS2017, N-BaIoT, and CICIoT2023. Smart healthcare is mentioned only as a potential application, and the study does not evaluate IoMT traffic, medical devices, patient-monitoring systems, hospital networks, or healthcare-specific attack scenarios. Therefore, it does not satisfy IC1.
